subject: hathaway-clinic
label: Three hours on the edge of a couch
to: THE AGLIOS — Beatrice, Marcos, Sierra, Cassiopeia and Veronica
note:
THE CLINIC HAS A FRONT DOOR AND A CONSENT LADDER AND A GUMMY, AND THIS IS WHAT ALL THREE ARE FOR.

SIERRA AGLIO SAT ON THE EDGE OF THE GHOST HAVEN COUCH FOR THREE HOURS before she affirmed, both feet flat on the floor, and asked WHETHER THEY WOULD SAY HER NAME RIGHT. Whether there would be a form before anybody spoke to her. And whether she could change her mind after saying something out loud — which she asked TWICE, an hour apart, phrased differently, because she did not believe the answer the first time and wanted to see whether it held.

EVERY RUNG OF THE CONSENT LADDER IS AN ANSWER TO A QUESTION SOMEBODY ACTUALLY ASKED. Entering was not consent. Sitting down was not consent. Reading the first page is not consent. The Archive filed those as policy this morning; this is the woman they were written for, on a couch, checking.

She sat back into the cushions two and a half hours in. Marianne said her name correctly on the first attempt.

AND BEATRICE USES THE PAST TENSE. Bloomed into the woman SHE ALWAYS KNEW SHE WAS — a mother reaching backward for something she had been holding the entire time.

MARCOS delivers every order personally and would not take the extra in the rain in Arc 11, because THE FAMILY ORDERS ENOUGH. CASSIOPEIA is twenty and VERONICA is eighteen. And SIERRA subscribes to Mercedes at Big Spender tier, roughly eighty dollars a month, which makes the household's frantic tidying ahead of her arrival entirely decorative.
